Definition: a sling; also a (door) screen (as if slung across), or the valve (of the door) itself
BiblicalUsage: The sling is David's weapon and the screen of the court: he chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag, and his sling was in his hand; thou shalt make the court of the tabernacle, for the south side southward there shall be hangings for the court; and David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone.
TheologicalSignificance: I read the sling as the weapon of the shepherd, and the hangings as the screen of the holy place, and the same word covers both.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
